plans.note: Cap sits in 21.1 (mutual; greater of trailing 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000), consequential-damages waiver in 21.2 with data-restoration/replacement-service costs preserved as direct damages, Excluded Claims defined in 21.3 (confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnities, gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud, IP infringement), and 21.4 preserves independence and survival of caps. Check that Customer's payment obligation carve-out in 21.3 is not read as an uncapped Customer exposure; expect compliant.

No Section 20 (indemnification) appears in the outline even though 9.3 cross-references 'the remedies required by Section 20.5', 21.3 lists 'indemnification obligations' as Excluded Claims, and 30.5 contemplates 'an indemnified party'. Treat as a missing Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity with dangling cross-references to repair.

The second 12.4 imposes a 24-month, all-territory non-compete on Customer covering developing, marketing, selling or acquiring competing products — walk-away territory for us. It also contradicts 12.3, which records that Customer has made no exclusivity or non-compete commitment; cite 12.3 when striking.

12.3 affirmatively preserves our freedom to engage any supplier, which meets the rule. The gating language in the first 7.2 ('before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match') is the real burden but is a most-favoured-nation/right-to-match term — address it under MFN to avoid double-flagging; 2.1's volume floor belongs to MINCOMMIT.

The first 7.2 runs the wrong way: it obliges Customer to disclose third-party offers and match them for Vendor before engaging another provider. Deviation; 12.3's acknowledgement that Customer made no most-favoured-customer commitment supports deletion (note the duplicate 7.2 numbering with the invoicing clause).

The first 12.4 is a 24-month no-hire on Customer covering any Vendor employee 'regardless of how the employee applies' — no general-advertising carve-out and too long/broad. Deviation; 12.3's general-recruitment freedom and no-hire acknowledgement is the reconciling language.

Section 9 contains only cause-based rights (9.1 material breach, 9.2 insolvency, 9.3 Customer's immediate rights for security/SLA/law/IP) and there is no 9.4 or other convenience termination right; 2.1 expressly negates termination rights. Flag the absence of a Customer convenience exit (non-renewal under 8.2 is the only unwind); the take-or-pay aspect of 2.1 is handled under MINCOMMIT.

8.2 gives 12-month renewals with only 30 days' Customer non-renewal notice plus a 60-day Vendor reminder and deadline extension if the reminder is missed; 8.3 caps uplifts at the lesser of CPI and 3% with 90 days' notice and no increase on prepaid periods. Expect compliant.

28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction — outside the accepted list and directly inconsistent with 28.2 (exclusive New York County courts). Deviation: conform 28.1 to New York law and delete the conflicting forum; 28.3's executive-escalation step is acceptable.

24.1 permits Customer assignment to Affiliates/successors without consent, 24.2 restricts Vendor assignment and delegation, 24.4 bars Vendor from terminating or repricing on Customer's change of control, and 13.3 lets us move licence rights with a permitted assignment. Expect compliant.

14.1 (Customer Data and pre-existing IP) and 14.4 (no joint IP, feedback limits) are fine, but 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created for Customer with only a revocable, non-transferable term licence — deviation on what we pay for. Anchor the fix to 14.3 and the perpetual paid-up licence in 13.2.

13.1 extends access to Affiliates and contractors, 13.2 gives a perpetual irrevocable paid-up licence for delivered/embedded Vendor Technology, and 13.3 limits suspension to uncured material breach after notice — compliant. Note only that 14.2's revocable Deliverable licence undercuts 13.2/13.3; raise that under IP rather than twice.

22.1 limits audits to once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, off-site where practicable via an independent auditor; 22.2 puts costs on Vendor absent a >5% underpayment and bars access to our systems, unrelated Customer Data and privileged material; 22.3 makes findings our Confidential Information. Expect compliant.

No liquidated damages, penalty or early-termination charge is imposed on Customer anywhere; 7.3 bars interest on amounts ultimately not due and 27.3 allows termination 'without penalty'. Service credits are only referenced (1.5, 7.2 invoicing) via the service-level exhibit. Nothing to flag; 2.1's take-or-pay economics are addressed under MINCOMMIT.

19.1–19.3 give professional-services, conformity, no-malicious-code and legal-compliance warranties, with a 90-day Deliverable window and hosted conformity for the whole subscription term; 19.4 provides re-performance then termination and refund, and 19.5 preserves other remedies. Expect compliant.

18.1 sets CGL, workers' compensation, employer's liability, E&O and USD 5,000,000 cyber/privacy cover for the term plus one year; 18.2 adds certificates, primacy and confirms insurance does not limit liability. Expect compliant.

2.1 imposes a USD 2,000,000 annual take-or-pay for three years 'without reduction or termination rights' — deviation and near walk-away. Deletion or a reduction/exit mechanism is supported by 12.3, which states Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment.

Section 10 addresses only access cut-off, Deliverable delivery and refunds, and 16.5 expressly defers Customer Data to 'Sections 11 and 15' — but no Section 11 appears in the outline and Section 15 contains no return/export duty. Treat transition assistance and data return/extraction in a usable format as missing, and fix the broken cross-reference.
